rules.rationale: Ionic halides without partly filled d states have the widest gaps; strong electronegativity contrast maximizes valence-conduction separation.
Main-group oxides are insulators; deep O 2p valence bands and empty s conduction states give large gaps.
Partially filled d manifolds insert mid-gap bands, systematically shrinking measured optical gaps.
Heavier chalcogen anions raise valence-band maxima covalently, yielding narrow semiconducting gaps; consistent with their high source refractive index.

skill.hypothesis: Ionicity and closed-shell cation chemistry, not transferred dielectric magnitudes, drive experimental band gap. May fail for lanthanide f-state compounds or halides reported with defect-narrowed gaps.
